## The contradiction inside a single row

**`bills-api`** — `est_sections = 6,535`, `est_is_confirmed = true`, and its own note reads:

> V25 §4: list:{billId} rows for 3919 bills → one section per publication PDF. OPL v3.0. est is the V21 placeholder; rebaseline at drain (per-PDF universe is much larger — bill 3774 alone = 267 PDFs).

The note says unmeasured. The flag says confirmed. The email read the flag.

**`scottish-courts`** — `est_sections = 13,070`, `est_is_confirmed = true`, and its own note reads:

> V27 §2: API unblocked via Origin/Referer-gated search; ROUGH order-of-magnitude only (~700 published opinions/yr since ~1998, unmeasured — search API blocked, old archive 404s). Replace with measured universe at unblock.

The note says unmeasured. The flag says confirmed. The email read the flag.

## The six scripts that set a target from a count

`INGEST_LABELS_REPORT` named five. There is a sixth, and it is the most explicit:

| script | rule |
|---|---|
| `v19-rebaseline-final.ts` | `est := compiled` for 3 named corpora, `est_is_confirmed = true` |
| `v19-rebaseline-pwdata.ts` | `est := compiled` for every `pwdata%` corpus |
| `v19-align-p1.ts` | `est := compiled` for 2 named corpora |
| `v19-fix-si-residue.ts` | `est := compiled` for `si-pre-2010` |
| `v20-rebaseline-drains.ts` | `est := compiled` for 2 named corpora |
| **`v30-denominator-rebaseline.ts`** | **generic**: any corpus with an empty queue backlog → `est := compiled`, `confirmed = true` |

⚠ **`v30-denominator-rebaseline.ts` records why, and the why is the whole story.** Its header:

> *"Fixes the honest-denominator violation flagged this session: summed `corpus_targets.est_sections`
> (16.56M) had fallen below actual compiled sections (17.65M compiled …), and two corpora … had no
> `corpus_targets` row at all — a 'lie of omission'."*

The problem was correctly identified: the denominator was smaller than the numerator, which is
impossible for a real denominator. The remedy chosen was to set the denominator to the numerator.
That converts an obvious error into an invisible one, and it was applied deliberately, in a script
whose stated purpose was honesty.
